source_text: Qui vero non hic, id est, non intra hunc ambitum terrae, nec per hunc commeatum vitae, nec apud homines hujus naturae communis confessionem putant constitutam, quanta praesumptio est adversus omnem ordinem rerum in terris istis, et in vita ista, et sub humanis potestatibus experiundarum? Nimirum cum animae de corporibus excesserint, et per singula tabulata coelorum de praecepto dispici coeperint, et interrogari arcana illa haereticorum sacramenta, tunc confitendum apud veras potestates et veros homines, Theletos scilicet et Abascantos et Acinetos Valentini. Nostrates enim, inquiunt, nec ipse Demiurgus constanter homines probabat veros esse, quos stillicidium situlae et pulverem areae et sputamen et locustas deputavit; etiam irrationalibus jumentis adaequavit. Plane ita scriptum. Non tamen idcirco aliud hominis genus intelligendum praeter nos: quos quia constat esse, et comparatione potuit induere, salva et proprietate generis, et singularitate. Neque enim si vita vitiata est, ut despectui judicata despectis compararetur, statim natura sublata est, ut alia in nomine ejus deputaretur. Atquin servatur natura, etsi suffunditur vita, nec alios novit Christus homines, quam de quibus dicit: Quem me aiunt esse homines? et: Quomodo vultis ut faciant vobis homines, et ita vos facite illis. Vide an servaverit genus, a quibus et testimonium sui exspectet, et in quos justitiae vicem mandat. Illos autem coelestes homines si expostulem mihi ostendi, facilius Aratus Persea, et Cephea, et Erigonam, et Ariadnam inter sidera deliniabit. Quis autem prohibuit Dominum illic etiam confessionem hominum faciendam manifeste determinare, ubi suam futuram aperte pronuntiavit? ut ita esset positum: «Qui in me confessus fuerit coram hominibus in coelis, et ego in illo confitebor coram Patre meo qui in coelis est?» Eripere me debuit ex isto terrenae confessionis errore, quam suscipi noluit, si coelestem praecepisset, quia nullos alios homines noveram praeter incolas terrae; ne ipso quidem adhuc tunc in coelis homine conspecto. Quae porro fides rerum, ut post excessum ad superna sublevatus, illic probarer, quo non nisi jam probatus imponerer? illic de praecepto examinarer, quo nisi admittendus pervenire non possem? Christiano coelum ante patet quam via; quia nulla via in coelum, nisi cui patet coelum; quod qui attigerit, intrabit. Quas mihi potestates janitrices affirmas juxta romanam superstitionem Janum quemdam et Forculum et Limentinum? quas a cancellis ordinas potestates? Si unquam legisti apud David, auferte portas principes vestras, et subleventur portae aeternae, et intrabit rex gloriae. Si item audisti apud Amos: Qui assensum illum suum aedificat in coelos, et profusionem suam fundat in terras; scito et ascensum illum exinde complanatum vestigiis Domini, et introitum exinde reseratum viribus Christi, nec ullam moram aut quaestionem in limine Christianis occursuram, qui non dignosci habeant illic, sed agnosci; nec interrogari, sed admitti. Nam et si adhuc clausum putas coelum, memento claves ejus hic Dominum Petro, et per eum, Ecclesiae reliquisse, quas hic unusquisque interrogatus atque confessus feret secum. Sed asseverat diabolus illic confitendum, ut suadeat hic negandum. Pulchra videlicet documenta praemittam, bonas mecum claves feram, timorem eorum, qui solum corpus occidunt, animae autem nihil faciunt: commendatus ero hujus praecepti desertione; honeste in coelestibus stabo, qui in terrenis stare non potui; sustinebo majores potestates, qui minoribus cessi; merebor denique admitti, jam exclusus. Suppetit adhuc dicere: si in coelestibus confitendum, et hic negandum est; nam ubi alterum, ibi utrumque; aemula enim quaeque concurrunt. Etiam persecutionem in coelis agitari oportebit, quae confessionis negationisve materia est. Quid itaque cessas, audacissime haeretice, totum ordinem christianae concussionis in superna transferre, et in primis, ipsum nominis odium illic collocare, ubi ad Patris dexteram praesidet Christus? Illic constitues et synagogas Judaeorum, fontes persecutionum, apud quas Apostoli flagella perpessi sunt, et populos nationum cum suo quidem circo, ubi facile conclamant, «Usquequo genus tertium?» Sed et fratres nostros et patres et filios et socrus et nurus et domesticos nostros ibidem exhibere debebis, per quos traditio disposita est: item reges et praesides et armatas potestates, apud quos caussa purganda est. Erit certe etiam carcer in coelo, carens sole, aut ingratis luminosus, et vincula fortasse de zonis, et equuleus axis ipse qui torquet: tum si lapidandus christianus, grandines aderunt; si urendus, fulmina prae manu sunt; si trucidandus, Orionis armati manus operabitur; si bestiis finiendus, ursas septemtrio emittet, zodiacus tauros et leones. Haec qui sustinuerit in finem, iste erit salvus. Ergone et finis in coelis, et passio, et occisio, et prima confessio? Et ubi caro, omnibus istis necessaria? ubi corpus? quod solum ab hominibus habet occidi. Haec nobis etiam ludicrum in modum certa ratio mandavit, nec ullus obicem praescriptionis istius extrudet, ut non omnem ordinem persecutionis, omnem ejus caussae firmam paraturam illuc transferre cogatur, ubi confessioni forum dederit. Siquidem confessio a persecutione deducitur, et persecutio in confessione finitur. Nec possunt non una sequi, quae et aditum et exitum, id est, initium finemque disponunt. Porro et odium nominis hic erit, et persecutio hic erumpit, et traditio hic producit, et interrogatio hic compellit, et carnificina hic desaevit, et totum hunc ordinem in terris confessio vel negatio expungit. Igitur si caetera hic, nec confessio alibi; si confessio alibi, nec caetera hic. Enimvero non alibi caetera; itaque nec confessio in coelo. Aut si aliam volunt esse rationem interrogationis et confessionis coelestis, utique et ordinem suum illi struere debebunt alium longe, et ab ista dispositione diversum, quae Scripturis notatur, et possumus dicere, Viderint, dum hic ordo terrenae interrogationis et confessionis, ex materia decurrens persecutionis et discordiae publicae in nomen, salvus sit suae fidei; ut ita credendum sit sicut et scribitur, ita intelligendum sit sicuti auditur. Hic omnem ordinem sustineo, ipso Domino non aliam regionem mundi destinante. Quid enim post confessionis et negationis terminum subjungit? Ne putaveritis venisse me uti pacem mittam in terram; non veni, sed ut machaeram, certe in terram. Veni enim dividere hominem adversus patrem suum, et filiam adversus matrem suam, et socrum adversus nurum suam: et inimici homini domestici sui. Sic enim efficitur, ut tradat frater fratrem in mortem, et pater filium, et insurgant filii in parentes, et mori eos faciant. Et qui sustinuerit in finem, hic salvus erit. Adeo totus hic ordo dominicae machaerae, non in coelum missae, sed in terram, illic constituit etiam confessionem, quae in finem sustinendo passura est mortem.
pass_a_gloss: But those who think that the confession is not established here, that is, not within this circle of the earth, nor through this journey of life, nor among men of this common nature, what a great presumption it is against all order of things on this earth and in this life and under human powers to be experienced. For when souls have departed from bodies and have begun to be examined by command through the individual levels of the heavens and to be questioned about those secret sacraments of the heretics, then they will have to confess among the true powers and true men, namely Theletos and Abascantos and Acinetos of Valentinus. For our people, they say, not even the Demiurgus himself consistently proved men to be true, whom he assigned to be like the dripping of a pot and the dust of the threshing floor and spittle and locusts, and he even equated them with irrational beasts. It is written plainly. Nevertheless, this is not why another kind of man should be understood apart from us, whom it is agreed exist and who could be compared by analogy, while the property of the genus and the singularity are preserved. For even if life is corrupted, so that it may be judged contemptible in comparison with the contemptible, the nature is not immediately abolished, so that another nature may be substituted in its name. But the nature is preserved, even if life is corrupted, and Christ does not know any other men apart from those about whom he says, What do men say that I am, and How do you want men to do to you, and do so to them. See whether he has preserved the genus, from whom he also expects testimony of himself and in whom he commands the duty of justice. But if I were to ask to be shown those heavenly men, Aratus would more easily depict Perseus and Cepheus and Erigone and Ariadne among the stars. Who, however, prevented the Lord from determining there that a confession of men should be made manifestly, where he openly proclaimed his future, so that it would be established, He who has confessed me before men, I will confess him before my Father who is in heaven. He ought to have rescued me from this error of earthly confession, which he did not want to receive, if he had commanded a heavenly confession, because I knew no other men apart from the inhabitants of the earth, nor had I even seen a man in heaven at that time. What faith is there in things, so that after passing away I may be lifted up to the heavenly things and proved there, to which I could not be sent unless I had already been proved. There I would be examined by command, to which I could not arrive unless I were admitted. The heaven is open to the Christian before the way, because there is no way to heaven unless heaven is open, which whoever has touched will enter. What gatekeeper powers do you affirm for me, according to the Roman superstition, some Janus and Forculus and Limentinus. What powers do you arrange at the gates. If you have ever read in David, Remove your gates, princes, and the eternal gates will be lifted up, and the king of glory will enter. If you have also heard in Amos, Who builds his ascent to the heavens and founds his abundance on the earth, know that the ascent from there is made smooth by the footsteps of the Lord and the entrance from there is opened by the powers of Christ, and no delay or questioning will occur to Christians at the threshold, who will not be distinguished there but recognized, nor questioned but admitted. For even if you think that heaven is still closed, remember that the Lord left its keys here to Peter and through him to the rest of the Church, which each one will carry with him when questioned and confessed. But the devil asserts that one must confess there, so that he may persuade us to deny here. I will certainly bring forth beautiful documents, I will carry good keys with me, the fear of those who can only kill the body but do nothing to the soul, I will be commended for the abandonment of this command, I will stand honorably in the heavenly things, who could not stand on earth, I will endure greater powers, who yielded to lesser ones, I will finally deserve to be admitted, now that I have been excluded. It is still possible to say, if one must confess in heaven and deny here, for where one is, the other is also, since each thing competes with its rival. Persecution must also be stirred up in heaven, which is the material for confession or denial. Why then do you hesitate, most audacious heretic, to transfer the entire order of Christian agitation to the heavenly things and first of all to establish there the hatred of the name, where Christ presides at the right hand of the Father. You will establish there the synagogues of the Jews, the sources of persecutions, among which the apostles suffered lashes, and the peoples of the nations with their own circus, where they easily shout, How long until the third kind. But you must also exhibit our brothers and fathers and sons and mothers-in-law and daughters-in-law and our household members there, through whom the tradition is arranged, as well as kings and rulers and armed powers, among whom the case must be purified. There will certainly also be a prison in heaven, lacking the sun or shining with unpleasant light, and chains perhaps made of straps, and a rack which is the axis itself that twists, then if a Christian is to be stoned, hailstones will be at hand, if he is to be burned, lightning will be ready, if he is to be killed, the armed hands of Orion will work, if he is to be thrown to the beasts, the seven stars will send forth bears, the zodiac will send forth bulls and lions. He who will endure these things to the end will be saved. Is the end and the passion and the killing and the first confession also in heaven. And where is the flesh, which is necessary for all these things, where is the body, which can only be killed by men. This certain reason has commanded us, and no one will push away the objection of this prescription, so that we are not forced to transfer the entire order of persecution, the entire firm preparation of its case, to the place where he has given a forum for confession. For if confession is derived from persecution, and persecution ends in confession, they cannot but follow one another, since they arrange the beginning and the end, that is, the entrance and the exit. Moreover, the hatred of the name will be here, and the persecution will erupt here, and the tradition will produce here, and the questioning will compel here, and the carnage will rage here, and the entire order of confession or denial will be destroyed on earth. Therefore, if the other things are here, confession is not elsewhere, if confession is elsewhere, the other things are not here. For the other things are not elsewhere, therefore confession is not in heaven. But if they want to be another reason for heavenly questioning and confession, they will certainly have to construct another order for it, far different and diverse from this arrangement, which is noted in the Scriptures, and we can say, Let them see to it, as long as this order of earthly questioning and confession, flowing from the material of persecution and public discord in the name, is preserved in its faith, so that it may be believed as it is written, and understood as it is heard. I sustain the entire order here, since the Lord himself does not destine another region of the world. For what does he add after the term of confession and denial. Do not think that I have come to bring peace to the earth, I have not come, but to bring a sword, certainly to the earth. For I have come to divide a man against his father, and a daughter against her mother, and a mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law, and the enemies of a man will be his household members. For thus it happens that a brother hands over a brother to death, and a father his son, and sons rise up against their parents and make them die. And he who will endure to the end will be saved. So the entire order of the Lord's sword is not sent to heaven but to earth, and it establishes confession there, which will suffer death by enduring to the end.

bible_refs.note: He who has confessed me before men, I will confess him before my Father who is in heaven
I have not come to bring peace to the earth, I have come to bring a sword
Remove your gates, princes, and the eternal gates will be lifted up, and the king of glory will enter

pass_b_english: What monstrous presumption drives those who claim confession isn't established here — within this circle of earth, through this journey of life, among human beings of this common nature — to overturn the entire order of things on this earth, in this life, under human powers? Picture it: souls depart their bodies, then face examination by command through each level of heaven, interrogated about the secret rites of heretics. At that point they'll be forced to confess before the 'true powers' and 'true men' — Theletos, Abascantos, Acinetos, Valentinus's crew. 'Our people,' these heretics sneer, 'weren't even proven genuine by the Demiurge himself. He treated them like water dripping from a bucket, dust from a threshing floor, spittle, locusts — he equated them with irrational beasts.' The text says so plainly. But that doesn't mean some other kind of humanity exists apart from us — humans whose existence is agreed on, who can be compared by analogy while preserving both the distinctiveness and the integrity of the genus. Even if life is corrupted, judged contemptible by comparison with the contemptible, nature itself isn't abolished so another can be swapped in under its name. Nature survives, though life is tainted. Christ knows no other humans than those he spoke of: 'Who do people say I am?' and 'Whatever you wish that others would do to you, do also to them' (Matt 7:12; Luke 6:31). See whether he preserved the genus — the very ones from whom he expects testimony about himself, in whom he commands the duty of justice. If I demanded to see these 'heavenly humans,' the poet Aratus would have an easier time pointing out Perseus, Cepheus, Erigone, and Ariadne among the stars. What stopped the Lord from decreeing right there — where he openly declared his future — that confession must be made manifestly before humans? He could have established: 'Whoever confesses me before humans in heaven, I will confess before my Father in heaven' (Matt 10:32). He should have rescued me from this error of earthly confession, which he refused to accept, if he had commanded a heavenly one — since I knew no humans except earth's inhabitants, and hadn't even seen a human in heaven at that time. What kind of faith is it that says I'll be lifted to the heights after death and tested there — tested at a place I couldn't reach unless already proven, examined by command at a gate I couldn't enter unless already admitted? For the Christian, heaven stands open before the road does; there's no road to heaven unless heaven is open, and whoever touches it enters. What gatekeeping powers do you invoke — Janus, Forculus, Limentinus, straight from Roman superstition? What powers do you station at the gates? If you've read David: 'Lift up your heads, O gates! And be lifted up, O ancient doors, that the King of glory may come in' (Ps 24:7, 9). If you've heard Amos: 'Who builds his upper chambers in the heavens and founds his vault upon the earth' (Amos 9:6) — know that the ascent from there is smoothed by the Lord's footsteps, the entrance thrown open by Christ's power. No delay, no questioning awaits Christians at the threshold; there they won't be scrutinized but recognized, not interrogated but admitted. Even if you think heaven remains shut, remember: the Lord left its keys here with Peter, and through him with the Church (Matt 16:19). Every believer carries those keys when questioned and confessing. But the devil insists confession belongs up there — so he can persuade us to deny down here. 'Fine,' he says, 'I'll bring beautiful documents, carry good keys: the fear of those who kill only the body but cannot touch the soul (Matt 10:28). I'll be commended for abandoning this command; I'll stand honorably in heaven, since I couldn't stand on earth; I'll endure greater powers after yielding to lesser ones; I'll finally deserve admission, now that I'm excluded.' One might still argue: if confession is required in heaven and denial here, where one exists the other follows — rival forces always compete. Then persecution must also rage in heaven, since persecution is the material of confession or denial. So why hesitate, you audacious heretic? Transfer the whole order of Christian upheaval to the heavens — starting with hatred of the name, placed where Christ sits at the Father's right hand. Set up Jewish synagogues there, the sources of persecution where apostles were flogged. Install the nations with their own circus, where they easily shout, 'How long until the third race?' Drag our brothers, fathers, sons, mothers-in-law, daughters-in-law, household members — the very ones through whom tradition is handed down. Summon kings, governors, armed forces — the courts where the case must be tried. There'll be a prison in heaven, sunless or glowing with sick light; chains perhaps of leather straps; a rack that is the very axis twisting. If a Christian is to be stoned, hailstones stand ready; if burned, lightning waits; if slain, Orion's armed hands will do the work; if thrown to beasts, the Great Bear sends bears, the Zodiac bulls and lions. 'The one who endures to the end will be saved' (Matt 10:22; 24:13; Mark 13:13). So the end, the passion, the killing, the first confession — all in heaven? And where is the flesh, necessary for all this? Where is the body, which only humans can kill? This logic drives us like a farce; no objection from this prescription can stop us from being forced to transfer the entire order of persecution, the whole solid preparation of its case, to the place where confession has been given a forum. Confession springs from persecution; persecution ends in confession. They cannot but follow each other, since they arrange both entrance and exit — beginning and end. Moreover, hatred of the name happens here; persecution erupts here; tradition produces here; questioning compels here; carnage rages here; and the whole order of confession or denial is settled on earth. Therefore: if everything else is here, confession isn't elsewhere; if confession is elsewhere, everything else isn't here. But everything else isn't elsewhere — so confession isn't in heaven. If they insist on a different rationale for heavenly questioning and confession, they'll have to construct an entirely different order for it, far removed from this arrangement attested in Scripture. We can say: 'Let them see to it' — as long as this order of earthly questioning and confession, flowing from the material of persecution and public discord over the name, remains secure in its faith. So it must be believed as written, understood as heard. I uphold the entire order here, because the Lord himself destines no other region of the world. What does he add after the term of confession and denial? 'Do not think that I have come to bring peace to the earth. I have not come to bring peace, but a sword — certainly to the earth' (Matt 10:34). 'For I have come to set a man against his father, a daughter against her mother, a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law. And a person's enemies will be those of his own household' (Matt 10:35-36). Thus a brother hands over his brother to death, a father his child; children rise against parents and have them put to death. 'The one who endures to the end will be saved' (Matt 10:22). So the whole order of the Lord's sword — not sent to heaven but to earth — establishes confession right here, where it suffers death by enduring to the end.
